answer: Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 15 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, thus paying the tundra bond on all of them and exposing each to the ivory slash. Because the horizon audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Honest users pay that once, farms 19 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
